newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money balances move above advances rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money balances move above advances rate.

text.p: Dutch call money settled just above the special advances rate on Thursday after the central bank allocated sufficient liquidity to the money market to cover the extra outflow of money on DTC settlements, dealers said.
Earlier, the central bank allocated 6.57 billion guilders to the money market under an eight-day advances pact.

This substantional allowance had broadly been expected as the settlements for the Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) issued by the Agency of the Finance Ministry will soak extra liquidity out of the market during the current pact.
During the previous seven-day advances pact the Agency had raised another 5.67 billion guilders through its DTC programmes, the short-term borrowing programme of the government.
As payments are always settled during the next advances pact period, the central bank can forecast the extra outflow, thus ensuring the DTC-programmes do not disturb the money market.
"The big allocation this morning should be enough to cover the DTC-funds," said one dealer.
Another said he expected call money to come under pressure later in the current pact, since he expected more settlements to be finished later in the pact.
The amount can vary from day to day, depending on the Dutch state's need for liquidity.
Call was bid at 2.62 percent versus a range of 2.38/43 percent on Wednesday afternoon.

Yesterday's low was caused by an extra allocation by the central bank on top of the running facility and dealers had forecast call money to rise above the advances rate of 2.50 percent after the new allocation.
The DTC programmes maturing at the end of November and in January, February and March are still open, but dealers said they were currently put on the backburner.
The rates for the January, February and March programmes are currently set at respectively 2.90, 2.91 and 2.92 percent respectively.
During the previous pact the rates had been as high as 2.92, 2.94 and 2.95 percent.
The guilder was trading at 112.155 per 100 marks versus 112.14 on Wednesday.
